title: Fish and bird migration
notes: [Remember] Migration is the periodic, seasonal, two-way movement of animals between breeding and non-breeding habitats — distinct from one-way dispersal or permanent emigration.

[Remember] Fish migration: anadromous fishes move from sea to fresh water to breed (e.g. Hilsa ilisha ascending Terai rivers in monsoon); catadromous fishes move from fresh water to sea to breed (e.g. eels, Anguilla).

[Understand] Bird migration types: latitudinal or north–south (Siberian ducks wintering at Koshi Tappu and Chitwan), longitudinal, and altitudinal (pheasants and thrushes descending from hills to Terai in winter).

[Understand] Causes and triggers: breeding urge, food scarcity, shortening photoperiod, falling temperature and hormonal change; navigation uses the sun compass, star patterns, Earth's magnetic field and geographical landmarks.
[Apply] Contrast table — anadromous vs catadromous (direction, breeding ground, one example each); resident vs migratory vs partial-migrant birds with one Nepali example of each.

[Analyze] Advantages (safe breeding grounds, abundant seasonal food) versus costs (enormous energy demand, predation, barriers such as dams and habitat loss); homing instinct and ringing/banding studies as evidence.

[Evaluate/Create] NEB answer frame: define migration → classify fish and bird types → causes and navigation → Koshi Tappu/Chitwan and Terai-river examples → one advantage–cost line → labelled route sketch.
confusion: Migration is two-way and seasonal; one-way dispersal or permanent emigration is NOT migration.
Anadromous = sea → river to breed; catadromous = river → sea to breed — do not swap the arrows.
Altitudinal migration (hills ↔ Terai) is still migration even though the distance is short.
Homing instinct and banding studies prove return journeys; do not claim birds 'get lost and stay'.
practice: Draw the anadromous vs catadromous arrow table from memory in under 3 minutes.
Recall card: triggers → navigation cues → one Nepali site → one cost.
universalFacts: Migration is classified by direction and distance; examples earn full marks only with the breeding ground named.
Nepal's Koshi Tappu and Chitwan wetlands are classic wintering-ground examples for Siberian migrants.
Anadromous vs catadromous is a favourite 2-mark contrast — arrows plus one fish each.
examples: Hilsa ascending Terai rivers in monsoon to spawn (anadromous).
Siberian ducks wintering at Koshi Tappu, returning north in spring (latitudinal bird migration).
Pheasants descending from high hills to lower valleys in winter (altitudinal migration).
practiceQuestions: Differentiate anadromous and catadromous fish migration with one example of each. (3)
Describe bird migration with its causes, navigation and two Nepali examples. (5)
keyPoints: Koshi Tappu/Chitwan examples plus route sketch
summary: Fish and bird migration: periodic two-way movement; anadromous vs catadromous fishes, latitudinal and altitudinal birds, causes, navigation, Koshi Tappu and Terai-river examples, advantage–cost balance.

mcqs.question: Hilsa ascending Terai rivers in monsoon to breed is an example of:
mcqs.explanation: Anadromous fishes move from sea to fresh water to breed; Hilsa ascending rivers in monsoon is the NEB classic.

mcqs.question: Siberian ducks wintering at Koshi Tappu demonstrate:
mcqs.explanation: North–south seasonal movement between breeding and wintering grounds is latitudinal migration.

mcqs.question: Which navigation cue is used by migratory birds?
mcqs.explanation: Birds navigate by sun compass, star patterns, magnetic field and landmarks.
